content_sections.body: Ask What time is it? For a whole hour, answer It is + number + o'clock. Use at before a time when you say when an action happens.
content_sections.title: Whole-hour time

content_sections.body: Tara gets up at seven o'clock. She eats breakfast at eight o'clock. She studies at nine o'clock. She goes home at four o'clock. This is a fictional routine written for this lesson.
content_sections.title: Tara's simple day

items.explanation: Use at before a clock time.

exercises.prompt: Write a four-sentence real or fictional routine with four whole-hour times.
exercises.rubric: Includes four clear routine actions.; Uses at before each time.; Forms whole-hour expressions with o'clock.; Keeps the routine in a logical order.

objectives: Tell and ask about simple whole-hour times.
Combine time and routine language in a short description.

constraints: Use only numbers one through ten and Unit 2 routine verbs.
Do not use external text, audio, or media.
listening.goal: Practise the listening target for this lesson.
listening.instruction: Read an original four-sentence daily schedule using whole-hour times. Keep the schedule hidden and ask two questions, one at a time, about an action and its time. Reveal the script afterward.

constraints: If no learner audio is available, state NOT_ASSESSED and provide a spoken model only where supported.
Do not score a typed response as pronunciation.
pronunciation.goal: Practise the pronunciation target for this lesson.
pronunciation.instruction: Model seven o'clock, eight o'clock, and at nine o'clock. Ask the learner to repeat and then say one full routine sentence with a time.

constraints: Use no more than five tutor turns.
Focus feedback on at, o'clock, and routine verbs.
speaking.goal: Practise the speaking target for this lesson.
speaking.instruction: Ask the learner what they do at two whole-hour times. Accept a real or fictional routine, then ask the learner to ask you What time do you ...? and answer as a fictional character.

constraints: Do not produce a full replacement schedule.
Keep feedback within the first ten pilot lessons.
writing.goal: Practise the writing target for this lesson.
writing.instruction: Ask for a four-sentence real or fictional daily schedule with whole-hour times. Wait for the draft, give up to three targeted comments, and ask the learner to revise one sentence.

title: My Simple Day
